tess: FYI I hit a bundler/runtime oddity while converting our Next sample to rollup+esbuild for an edge build. Node dev + SSR work fine but deployed edge shows duplicated Authorization header on retries.

omar: is that the same comma-separated dup we've seen?

tess: yup. logs: 
```
[redwood] auth failed: 401
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer BAD
Retrying...
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer BAD, Authorization: Bearer BAD
```

jia: which runtime + bundler options?

tess: rollup 3 + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve + esbuild for transforms, target=es2022, deployed to Cloudflare Pages (workers-v8). I tried both named ESM import and default import: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` reproduces; `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` sometimes does not.

omar: that discrepancy is interesting. Packaging maybe: exports map or interop wrapper for named vs default.

tess: repro steps I committed to a tiny branch: 
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps -b edge-rollup-repro-24802
2) cd next-rollup-edge
3) npm ci
4) REDWOOD_API_KEY=wrong npm run build:edge && npm run preview:edge
5) curl -v http://localhost:8787/api/chat

handler: 
```ts
// src/pages/api/chat.ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const resp = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hello' });
  const txt = await resp.text();
  res.status(200).send(txt);
}
```

miguel: we've seen similar with other bundlers. Quick debug: does changing retry to clone headers explicitly help? e.g. `const headers = new Headers(origReq.headers || {}); headers.set('Authorization', token); new Request(origReq, { headers })`

tess: I patched it in node_modules locally and the duplication stopped under miniflare/cloudflare preview. So defensive clone helps.

jia: good. But we should not rely on ad-hoc node_modules edits. Two separate root causes likely: (1) our retry code assumes fetch cloning semantics across environments, (2) bundler transforms / minification can cause helper state to be shared. I hit nondeterministic behavior when terser/minify=true because closure order changes.

omar: also TS DX: VSCode intellisense fails to show overloads for createClient when importing the ESM entry in this project. If I require dist/cjs it works. I suspect our package.json exports lack a types path for the ESM entry.

tess: exactly. I filed sdk#462 with repro and logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/462

ci-bot: queued job devex/edge-rollup-repro (#612) - matrix: cloudflare/workers-v8, wrangler-miniflare, vercel-edge.

miguel: action list: 
- tess: push the minimal repro branch (done), include exact rollup config + netlify/vercel snippets (ETA today).
- jia: open PR to make retry create fresh Headers for each retry and add unit tests (ETA tomorrow).
- omar: PR to package.json exports to point types -> add an explicit "types" entry for the ESM import path, plus a tiny TS compile check in CI (ETA EOD).

jia: I'll also add an integration that builds with rollup+terser and runs the bundle under our worker shims to catch minification-induced closures.

tess: one more odd observation: switching to default import avoids dup in some cases. This could help narrow whether it's our CJS interop helper (the wrapper that provides `.default`) causing a shared Headers instance. I logged the experiment in the repro README.

omar: good troubleshooting. If the clone fix passes the CI matrix we'll consider a patch release. Also add a CHANGELOG note describing the edge/runtime header-clone fix and the types export improvement.

ci-bot: job devex/edge-rollup-repro (#612) started...

tess: thanks all, will follow up with CI results and link the PRs here. :rocket:
